item.title: Total construction starts move lower in July
item.description: PRISM Sustainability in the Built Environment Total construction starts fell 3% in July to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of $854.8 billion, according to Dodge Data & Analytics. There were few bright spots during the month, with all three sectors (residential, nonresidential building and nonbuildings) moving lower in July. item.description: PRISM Sustainability in the Built Environment New York City’s Crotona Park’s arched entry to the pool building and play center in the Bronx features a newly reconstructed pair of 80-foot-tall clock towers capped with four-sided glass block “lanterns.” Completed in March 2021, the new lanterns were designed, engineered and fabricated by EXTECH/Exterior Technologies, Inc., and installed by Sandhu Contracting, Inc. item.title: Stantec to provide engineering services for Western Australia’s first comprehensive city centre university campus
item.description: PRISM Sustainability in the Built Environment Stantec was selected as lead engineer for the Edith Cowan University (ECU) City in Perth. item.title: ACI Concrete Convention transitions to fully virtual
item.description: PRISM Sustainability in the Built Environment Engineers, contractors, educators, manufacturers, and material representatives will convene virtually from October 17-21, 2021, at the ACI Concrete Convention, the world’s gathering place for advancing concrete. Originally scheduled as a hybrid event in Atlanta, GA, and online, the event will now be fully virtual. item.title: HGA-engineered elementary school becomes first Net Zero Energy school in Wisconsin
item.description: PRISM Sustainability in the Built Environment The Oregon School District joins an elite group of forward-looking national organizations with their new Forest Edge Elementary School. Completed in 2020, the 126,580 square foot facility has officially become the first Net Zero Energy (NZE) school in Wisconsin. item.title: PRISM winds down
item.description: PRISM Sustainability in the Built Environment We have made the difficult decision to wind down PRISM Sustainability in the Built Environment. We sincerely thank our readers and writers for their amazing contributions over the last five and a half years. It has certainly been the best of times mixed in with some not-so-great times.
